Moreno and Mossio state their programme: the organism, not natural selection, is biology's central idea; its core is a closure of constraints, which they say fundamentally differs from the process loops and self-organisation of dissipative structures, and which grounds teleology, normativity and function. With regulation and agency, closure makes an autonomous system, an organism; ecosystems meet only closure. The arguments are announced for chapters 1–7, which this reading does not cover. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1440](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1440.md) | Rung & Madden — Experimental reductions of delay discounting | A systematic review and category-wise meta-analysis of 92 papers that tried to lower delay discounting without drugs or lesions. Most kinds of manipulation worked, learning-based ones such as bundling and delay fading best. Clinical interventions moved discounting little, and mindfulness and ACT, two studies, only at trend level (g = 0.32, p = .06). Mediation was almost never tested, so how any manipulation lowers discounting is unknown. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1454](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1454.md) | Flynn, Kanerva & Bhadkamkar — SDM principles and operation | Kanerva and co-authors state SDM's critical distance in words and do not derive it: a cue within it converges on the stored pattern under iterated reads, a cue beyond it wanders and may settle on another pattern, the distance shrinks as the memory fills, and in a sparsely filled memory it is below the sum of the write and read radii. For single patterns convergence and divergence are "easy to distinguish in practice"; for stored sequences they are not. The rest of the report is a hardware design. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1462](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1462.md) | Chen, Lau, Mendel, Wei & Murfet — dynamical versus Bayesian transitions in TMS | In Elhage et al.'s toy model of superposition with two hidden dimensions, regular k-gons are critical points of a closed-form population loss, and their local learning coefficients predict, through the free energy formula, a Bayesian phase transition from the 5-gon to the 6-gon near n = 600 that MCMC confirms. SGD trajectories plateau at the same critical points and move to lower loss and higher estimated complexity. The paper's Bayesian antecedent hypothesis is one-directional, that training's transitions have Bayesian counterparts; it says outright that there is "no necessary relation" between the two kinds, and its main Bayesian transition, 5 → 6, was never seen in training. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1472](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1472.md) | Falasco & Esposito — macroscopic stochastic thermodynamics | Builds macroscopic stochastic thermodynamics from Markov jump processes with local detailed balance. Under extensive rates and potentials, a deterministic dynamics emerges whose Lyapunov function is the quasi-potential I_ss, and a large-deviation theory of fluctuations around it. Transition rates between attractors go as e^{−VΔI_ss} and are bracketed by the entropy produced along relaxation and escape paths; the bracket closes only near detailed balance. Gaussian-noise Langevin equations mis-estimate both the barriers and the entropy production. Read for those parts and the Schlögl example; field theory and two of three applications not read. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1486](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1486.md) | Massumi — The Principle of Unrest | Interviews and an essay in activist philosophy. Movement is qualitative relational transformation, and capitalism an ontopower feeding on "bare activity". Micropolitics aims at "a maximally inclusive co-patterning of contrasting tendencies" (p. 64), an aesthetic ideal that affirms discord rather than resolving it. The parent paper's quotation is exact; it turns the ideal into a description of organizational becoming. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1499](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1499.md) | Metzinger — The Elephant and the Blind | More than 500 meditators' retrospective reports of "pure awareness", from a survey of 1,403 people in 57 countries, are offered as evidence that consciousness occurs without time, self-location, an egoic self-model or a first-person perspective. Pure awareness is modelled as the top level of a nested active-inference hierarchy, "a highest-level but nonegoic self-model" of the organism's own epistemic openness. The book concedes that retrospective reports cannot show that a state was selfless when it happened, and its summary calls nonegoic consciousness "empirically established" all the same. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1504](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1504.md) | Heymann & Vanden-Eijnden — The geometric minimum action method | The Freidlin–Wentzell quasi-potential, a double minimization over paths and their duration, is rewritten as a single minimization over curves of a parametrization-free action, which has minimizers when the end points are equilibria and is computed by a string-method-like relaxation (gMAM). For a diffusion it is V = 2 inf ∫ \|b\| sin²(θ/2) ds. In gradient systems with identity noise the most likely transition paths are parallel to the drift; in the nongradient Maier–Stein model they depart from the heteroclinic orbit once the drift is far enough from gradient. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1505](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1505.md) | Lu, Gallagher, Michala, Fish & Lindsey — The Assistant Axis | Role vectors for 275 archetypes in Gemma 2 27B, Qwen 3 32B and Llama 3.3 70B span a low-dimensional persona space whose first component runs from fantastical roles to Assistant-like ones, with the default Assistant at one end; the contrast vector from it, the Assistant Axis, is largely present in base models. Steering along it modulates role-taking and persona jailbreaks. In synthetic multi-turn conversations the model's position along the axis is set mainly by the latest user message, and therapy-like and AI-philosophy conversations drift away from the Assistant; capping the projection cuts persona-jailbreak harm by about 60% without measured capability loss. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1524](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1524.md) | Chen, Arditi, Sleight, Evans & Lindsey — Persona vectors | Difference-of-means directions in the residual stream, extracted automatically from a trait's name and description, steer and monitor evil, sycophancy and hallucination in Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.1-8B. The shift that finetuning induces along a trait's vector correlates with the trait's expression afterwards (r = 0.76–0.97); steering against the vector, or towards it during training, limits the shift; and projecting training data onto the vector flags data that will induce the trait. Prompt-time monitoring works mainly between prompt types. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1532](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1532.md) | Juarrero — Context Changes Everything | Juarrero's restatement of her 1999 constraint account as a general natural philosophy, self-described "speculative metaphysics" (p. 32). Context-independent constraints take conditions away from equiprobability, context-dependent ones away from independence (Gatlin), and enabling constraints couple separate processes into coherent "interactional types" whose constitutive constraints double as governing, "second-order" constraints that hold components to a subregion of state space, top down, "as constraints, not efficient causes" (p. 25). Levels are demarcated by rate discontinuities, wholes are slower than parts, and inter-level control is lost when the rates converge (ch. 12, from Salthe and Allen and Starr). It adopts Montévil and Mossio's closure of constraints verbatim (pp. 93–94). It has no formal model of its own and does not discuss Kane, free will, chaos or contextual emergence. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1535](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1535.md) | Bishop — Chaos (SEP) | The 2024 revision of Bishop's SEP entry. Chaos is a property of deterministic models; unpredictability is not indeterminism. The sensitive-dependence argument that chaos amplifies quantum events is qualified: damping, negative local Lyapunov exponents and, in the brain, "parallel redundancy" may stop amplification. For Kane, sensitivity alone does not give incompatibilist freedom, and the incompatibilist must still show agents can "harness" indeterminism. §6.2–6.3 state Bishop's contextual emergence as an ontological account: larger-scale stability conditions that constrain and enable smaller-scale behaviour. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1536](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1536.md) | Scheffer et al. — Early-warning signals for critical transitions | A review of generic early-warning signals for critical transitions. At a fold bifurcation the dominant eigenvalue goes to zero, so recovery from small perturbations slows (critical slowing down). Under ongoing perturbation that shows as rising lag-1 autocorrelation and rising variance. Skewness and flickering are further signals, not caused by slowing down. Spatial systems add rising cross-correlation and specific pattern sequences. Evidence from climate, ecosystems, epilepsy, asthma and finance is reviewed. The signals mark proximity to a broad class of thresholds, not only catastrophic ones, so they do not say which kind; false positives and negatives are named. Cyclic and chaotic systems are "less well studied". | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1539](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1539.md) | Crowell, Beauchaine and Linehan — A biosocial developmental model of borderline personality | Linehan's biosocial theory as restated with her: emotion dysregulation, "heightened emotional sensitivity", inability to regulate intense responses and "slow return to emotional baseline", is the core, and cognitive dysregulation is among its consequences, "distorted information processing" and difficulty organizing toward "non-mood-dependent goals". Skimmed; read for the theory, not the biology. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1542](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1542.md) | Lake, Salakhutdinov & Tenenbaum — Human-level concept learning through probabilistic program induction | Bayesian Program Learning models handwritten characters as stochastic programs: types composed of strokes, sub-strokes from a learned library and relations; tokens from executing a type with motor noise; images from rendering tokens. Priors are fit to 30 background alphabets. On 20-way one-shot classification within 10 held-out alphabets, BPL erred 3.3% against people's 4.5%; lesions without learning to learn or without compositionality erred 11.0% and 14.0%. In four visual Turing tests, judges told BPL's exemplars and new characters from people's at about chance. Main text only; the model's details are in the unread Supplementary Materials. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1555](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1555.md) | Zhuk — A proof of the CSP dichotomy conjecture | Zhuk proves the CSP dichotomy for finite domains independently of Bulatov: for a finite language Γ on a finite set, CSP(Γ) is in P if a weak near-unanimity operation preserves Γ, NP-complete otherwise. The algorithm checks local consistency, reduces domains to absorbing subuniverses, centres or quotients, and in the linear case solves linear equations over prime fields. Read: the introduction, outline, definitions, the structural Theorem 5.1 with proof, and the conclusions; the main proofs not read. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1560](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1560.md) | Tatel — A meta-analysis of procedural skill retention and decay | A random-effects meta-regression of procedural skill retention, with retention interval in months as a continuous predictor, over 457 sources. Decline is linear: 0.08 SD a month for accuracy (829 effect sizes) and 0.06 for speed (267) and mixed (180). About half of training gains are lost after 6–9 months (accuracy), 12–15 (speed) and 9–12 (mixed). Practice opportunities in the interval slowed accuracy decline. Residual heterogeneity is large, the moderators far from definitive, and relearning during retention tests probably makes the estimates too low. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1562](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1562.md) | Freidlin & Wentzell — Random Perturbations of Dynamical Systems, front matter | Front matter only. The Introduction outlines the programme: limit theorems for small random perturbations of a dynamical system, of which the rough large-deviation results matter most, because the probabilities of rare events on finite intervals decide behaviour on infinite ones. An action functional S(ϕ) gives P{ρ(Xᵋ, ϕ) < δ} ≈ exp{−ε⁻²S(ϕ)}; the exit time from a domain is approximately exponential, and with several stable sets the stationary distribution concentrates on the one with the larger infimum of S for leaving it. The theorems themselves are in chapters not read. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1563](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1563.md) | Kaelbling, Littman and Cassandra — Planning and acting in partially observable stochastic domains | A restatement, for AI, of the operations-research theory of POMDPs that Smallwood and Sondik founded. The belief state, a distribution over hidden states updated by Bayes' rule, is a sufficient statistic, so control is an MDP over beliefs; the optimal finite-horizon value is the upper surface of one linear function per policy tree, hence piecewise-linear and convex. Information-gathering actions are valued in the same calculation as others, as the tiger problem shows. Exact solution is exponential in the worst case. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1567](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1567.md) | Guigues, Kleywegt and Nascimento — A Markov preparedness metric for ambulance selection and reassignment | Defines a station-level preparedness metric, the steady-state cost rate of a continuous-time Markov chain over a station's busy ambulances, and uses it inside one-step integer programs for choosing which ambulance to send (or whether to queue the call) and where a freed ambulance goes. In a Rio de Janeiro simulation the policy had lower mean allocation cost than nine published policies in most cases and was among the best on mean response time. Results skimmed; costs assumed; ADP policies not compared. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1568](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1568.md) | Botnan and Lesnick — An introduction to multiparameter persistence | A survey of multiparameter persistence. For two or more parameters the modules are of wild representation type, good barcodes need not exist, and the rank invariant is incomplete, so practice uses incomplete invariants and vectorizations. The interleaving distance extends the bottleneck distance, is stable and, over prime fields, universal, but is NP-hard to compute. Read: §1, §§3.3–3.4, §§4.1–4.2, §6.1 to Theorem 6.9, §8.1 and the start of §8.2. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1572](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1572.md) | Bulatov — A dichotomy theorem for nonuniform CSPs | Bulatov proves the CSP dichotomy for finite domains: every CSP(Γ) over a finite constraint language on a finite set is in P or NP-complete, P exactly when the polymorphisms include a weak near-unanimity operation. The new part is the algorithm, which combines local consistency, a new non-local condition (block-minimality) and the few-subpowers algorithm. Read: the introduction and §§2–3.2's opening; the ~80 pages of proof were not read. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1576](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1576.md) | Bogetoft and Hougaard — Rational inefficiencies | Measured technical inefficiency, slack, is read as a rational choice: an organization valuing off-the-job profit and on-the-job slack uses an allocatively efficient underlying plan under price-based control and a technically efficient one under restriction-based control, and takes the rest as profit and slack. Observed inputs then reveal, partially, how it trades profit against slack and one kind of slack against another. Since the gains from slack are unknown, inefficiency cannot be concluded to be waste; the line between valuable and non-valuable slack is left open. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1577](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1577.md) | van Leeuwaarden, Mathijsen and Zwart — Tutorial on the QED Halfin–Whitt regime | A tutorial on the Quality-and-Efficiency-Driven regime. Staffing s = λ + β√λ adds headroom of the order of the load's fluctuations; Halfin and Whitt showed that under this scaling, and only under it, the M/M/s delay probability has a limit strictly between zero and one, and that the scaled number in system tends to a diffusion. Utilization then tends to one while mean delay vanishes like 1/√s, the economies of scale of pooling, and the limits give staffing rules within one server of the exact optimum in the authors' examples. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1581](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1581.md) | Raussen — Connectivity of spaces of directed paths in concurrent computation | In the PV model of concurrency, shared resources of fixed capacity cut a forbidden region from the product of the processors' time intervals; executions are directed paths avoiding it, and d-homotopic executions give the same result. A spare capacity computed from the program text bounds the connectivity of every space of executions from below: zero at exactly the deadlocks, at least one excludes them, at least two makes all executions equivalent. Read: §1, §§2.1–2.2.1, §3.1, §3.4, §§4.1–4.2, §§5.3–5.4. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1583](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1583.md) | Mukhopadhyay et al. — Review of incident prediction, resource allocation and dispatch models | Read for §6.1. The seminal static coverage models, LSCP and MCLP, assume deterministic response, with a facility's resources always available; multiple coverage such as the double standard model mitigates unavailability but cannot rule out every covering facility being busy, which needs probabilistic models. MEXCLP assumes one busy probability for every facility and independence; MALP-I keeps equal busy probabilities, and MALP-II computes them from local demand. Later extensions relax independence, one through a hypercube queue. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1584](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1584.md) | Gopalan et al. — The connectivity of Boolean satisfiability | Classifies, by the constraint language alone, how hard it is to tell whether two solutions of a Boolean CNF(S)-formula with constants are joined by single-variable flips through solutions. For tight languages st-connectivity is in P, connectivity in coNP and diameter linear; otherwise both are PSPACE-complete and diameter can be 2^Ω(√n). Tight properly contains Schaefer, and the boundary cuts across Boolean clones. The hard side, read only in outline, is slightly wrong as stated: Schwerdtfeger moves it to "safely tight". | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1585](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1585.md) | Lawvere — Metric spaces, generalized logic, and closed categories | A generalized metric space is exactly a category enriched in [0, ∞] with ≥ as maps and + as tensor: the triangle inequality is composition and zero self-distance the identity. Symmetry and finiteness are not categorical and are dropped, since non-symmetric costs are natural. The 2002 commentary adds that free V-categories on V-graphs are path closures and that profunctor composition is Bellman–Fenchel convolution. Read: the commentary in full and the 1973 introduction by eye from the scan; the general theory not read. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1587](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1587.md) | Evans, Silverberg & Santangelo — Lattice mechanics of origami tessellations | A lattice theory of periodic origami: each degree-N vertex has N − 3 internal degrees of freedom with several configuration branches; vertices are joined through shared folds and a Bloch-wave ansatz gives a rigidity-like matrix. In the Miura-ori, with facet bending as extra folds, soft modes are localized at the edges with an analytic decay length, checked on an 8 × 8 paper sheet with an indenter and with reversible pop-through defects; degrees of freedom scale with the perimeter. Linear, one ground state. It does not state the 2014 paper's bistable cells or crystal-defect analogy. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1588](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1588.md) | Connelly and Whiteley — Second-order rigidity and prestress stability for tensegrity frameworks | For frameworks of bars, cables and struts, first-order rigidity implies prestress stability, which implies second-order rigidity, which implies rigidity, and examples show none of these reverses, even for bar frameworks. Whether a first-order flex extends to second order is decided by a Farkas-type test over all the proper self-stresses; with a one-dimensional cone of flexes or of stresses, second-order rigidity and prestress stability coincide. Read in part: the long proofs and later examples were skipped. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1592](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1592.md) | Hopkins — Parallel flexure design via Freedom and Constraint Topologies (master's thesis) | The founding statement of FACT for parallel flexures. Motions are twists, constraints wrenches, and the freedom space is the null space of the constraint wrenches; each freedom space is linked one to one with a constraint space, and for ideal pure-force constraints the pairs fall into 26 types in six cases. A redundant constraint is one whose addition or removal leaves the freedom space unchanged while stiffness, load capacity and stability change, and the design procedure uses such constraints for stiffness and symmetry. Some motion sets cannot be had from constraints without unwanted extra freedoms. Elastomechanics, dynamics and actuation are out of scope. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1593](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1593.md) | Ignatov — Introduction to formal concept analysis | A summer-school tutorial whose theory sections restate Ganter & Wille's formal concept analysis: contexts, derivation operators forming an antitone Galois connection, closure operators, concepts, the complete concept lattice and the Basic Theorem, and attribute implications with their Armstrong rules and Duquenne–Guigues base, all with exercises in place of proofs. Read: the theory (pp. 1–10, 15–17) and the conclusion; the applications not read. It shows that A's demand–configuration Galois connection is exactly the derivation-operator connection of a formal context. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1596](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1596.md) | Hopkins — Flexure motion stages via Freedom, Actuation and Constraint Topologies (PhD thesis) | Extends FACT from parallel to serial flexures and from kinematics to actuation. With constraints of any pitch there are 50 freedom/constraint space types; only those inside a "parallel pyramid" can be built in parallel, and the rest need modules stacked in series, whose freedoms add. A serial system whose intermediate bodies keep freedoms is underconstrained and has poor dynamics. A twist–wrench stiffness matrix gives the actuation space, where linear actuators must act to drive the freedoms without parasitic error; it depends on the flexures' geometry and material, not on the freedom space alone. One experiment located the least-error actuator line near the predicted one. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1599](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1599.md) | Gerardi and Maestri — Dynamic contracting with limited commitment and the ratchet effect | A firm can offer a worker with a persistent private cost only one-period menus over a potentially infinite horizon; the worker may quit for good. Revealing a low cost forfeits future rent (the ratchet effect). Impatient parties still allow full learning for any prior; above a patience threshold separation with both types employed is impossible; as patience tends to one the outcome is unique, pooling forever with no learning below a prior threshold and firing the high-cost worker above it, both inefficient. With rehiring, a folk theorem restores near-commitment payoffs. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1604](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1604.md) | Chou, Chua, Teo and Zheng — Efficiency of the long chain and sparse structure | Analytical support for Jordan and Graves's chaining principle. Plants and products form a bipartite graph, and sales once demand is known are a max-flow. For balanced, identical systems with independent demand, the long chain keeps at least 89% (uniform) and 96% (normal) of full flexibility's expected sales as the system grows; in general a suitably sampled sparse structure comes within ε of full flexibility; with correlated demand a sparse structure can serve almost none of it. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1606](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1606.md) | Foschi, Hull and Ku — Closed-form kinematics of degree-4 origami vertices | Two algebraic equations in the tangents of half the folding angles, for opposite and for adjacent creases, describe the configuration space of any degree-4 rigid origami vertex, developable, elliptic or hyperbolic. They recover the flat-foldable relations and Huffman's, give new ones for general developable vertices, show in a worked example that the two folding modes are disconnected when the sector angles do not sum to 2π, prove a square-twist pouch bistable, and give a folding table with a single mode. Proofs in unread appendices. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1609](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1609.md) | Vipond — Multiparameter persistence landscapes | The persistence landscape extended to modules indexed by Rⁿ: λ(k, x) is the largest radius over which k features persist in every positive direction through x. Stable under the interleaving distance; its weighted versions together determine the rank invariant of a finitely presented module; Banach-valued, so open to statistics. No complete discrete invariant exists for such modules, and the landscape sees only the rank invariant. Read: §§1–4 and 7; §§5–6 skimmed; appendices not read. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1613](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1613.md) | Schwerdtfeger — A computational trichotomy for connectivity of Boolean satisfiability | Shows, by examples and amended lemmas, that Gopalan et al.'s connectivity dichotomies for Boolean CSPs overlooked constraints with a repeated variable, which can destroy the component structure the easy side relies on, and restates their theorems with "safely tight" sets, closed under identification of variables. States, with the proof not read here, the trichotomy they conjectured: connectivity in P for CPSS sets, coNP-complete for the other safely tight sets, PSPACE-complete otherwise. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1618](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1618.md) | Hua, Luo, Swersey and Wen — A geometrically convergent solution to spatial hypercube queueing models | Extends the exact hypercube queueing model to server-specific service rates, solved through a birth–death process and an equivalent reformulation that the authors prove converges at a geometric rate, and parallelizes it. Reported over 1,000 times faster than a sparse solver and over 500 times faster than simulation on EMS data; proofs and tables not checked here. Credits Larson (1974) with the model, the alternating hyperplane solution method and the TOUR algorithm. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1620](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1620.md) | Larson and Odoni — Urban Operations Research, the hypercube queueing model | The book's own statement of the hypercube queueing model, read in prose only. N distinguishable units, each busy or free, over a city split into Poisson-source atoms, with a fixed preference list for dispatch per atom; from the steady state, unit workloads, dispatch fractions by unit and atom, dispatches across response areas and travel times. Backup dispatching evens out unit workloads. The basic model evaluates response areas a user supplies and does not optimize them; exact solution grows as 2^N, and Larson's approximation reduces it to N equations. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1621](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1621.md) | de Oliveira, de Sá and Martins — Multi-period bi-objective ambulance location in Belo Horizonte | Read for its §2 survey of probabilistic ambulance-location models. MEXCLP maximizes expected coverage under uniform busyness and independent servers; MALP maximizes demand covered with reliability α, keeps independence and adds locally constrained service areas, but drops uniform availability by area-specific busy fractions; Sorensen and Church's LR-MEXCLP builds on both and answers their objection to MALP's α objective. The paper's own multi-period models and results were not read. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1626](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1626.md) | Cumberworth and Reinhardt — Models and simulations of structural DNA nanotechnology | Read in part. In the review's account of simulations, a staple's later domains bind within one structure without a second translational penalty, but each loop closed constrains the scaffold at an entropic cost that depends on binding order; small loops tend to close first, and a staple typically binds fully once started. Origami assembly is mostly downhill and needs no nucleation barrier, unlike DNA bricks, though one can be designed in; blocking is rare at typical staple concentrations. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1644](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1644.md) | Sobczak — Investigations of the DNA origami folding process (dissertation) | Gel and SYBR Green assays show 3D DNA origami folding cooperatively in a structure-specific window of about 5 °C, foldable at constant temperature within it, and melting 5–10 °C higher within seconds while folding takes minutes to hours. Cooperativity spans connected subdomains; staple concentration and internal routing shift the window and the rate, routing by more than 100-fold at fixed shape and composition. A kinetic model, partly read, blames spurious short binding for low-temperature inhibition, and a short-domain design folds only when cooled fast to its folding temperature. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1647](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1647.md) | Ostrom, Gibson, Shivakumar and Andersson — Aid, incentives and sustainability | Sida's commissioned institutional analysis of its own aid. Predictable help sets up a Samaritan's dilemma: the donor's dominant strategy is to help and the recipient's best reply is low effort, so the recipient's own upkeep falls and donor-built assets decay and are rebuilt from outside (Kafue Gorge). Benefits outlast the aid only with beneficiary ownership in four dimensions, demand, own contribution, benefit and a say over continuation, which the authors call necessary but not sufficient. The evidence is theory, interviews and five short illustrative cases; no counterfactual. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1658](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1658.md) | Mauss — Essai sur le don | Mauss's comparative essay on the gift, skimmed with its introduction, first chapter, the Northwest-coast section and its conclusion read in full. Gifts in archaic societies are voluntary in form and obligatory in fact, between collectivities, under three obligations: to give, to receive and to return. The Maori hau of the thing given seeks its origin; the potlatch is returned with interest on pain of lost face, rank and freedom. To accept without returning is to become client and servant. The conclusion carries this into modern morality: charity wounds, social insurance is a return owed to the worker, and the individual must still rely on himself. Interpretive, on second-hand ethnography. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1659](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1659.md) | Watson — Agency-customer interactions in condominial sewerage in seven Brazilian cities | Condominial sewerage in seven Brazilian cities over twelve years: in about half the cases as good as conventional sewers at a third to a quarter of the cost. Devolving feeder upkeep to residents' blocks rarely worked, and the agencies' retreat left a void; the systems lasted where agencies kept specialised, face-to-face maintenance, monitoring and education and answered organised residents, and decayed where agencies refused or neglected them. Qualitative, seven non-random cities; only operation and maintenance and the conclusion were read. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1680](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1680.md) | LaVoice — Slum clearance and the neighbourhoods cleared, read from a short draft | About 200 Title I projects funded before 1965 in 28 large US cities, geocoded to census tracts for 1940–2000. Among similarly blighted tracts, black neighbourhoods were two to three times as likely to be cleared. Against slums in cities with limited participation, cleared tracts kept about 13% lower population density, 12% lower housing density and a 16% lower black share for decades, with rents up about a quarter and incomes up for a decade and then fading; the draft gives the income gain as 18% and as 16% without reconciling them. Within cities, rents in untreated low-income tracts rose in step, and a spatial-equilibrium model reads the lowest-income households city-wide as made worse off. The displaced are not tracked and social ties are not measured. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1690](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1690.md) | Davis and Weinstein — A search for multiple equilibria in urban industrial structure, read in part from the NBER working paper | A threshold-regression test of unique against multiple equilibria, applied to the Allied bombing of Japan for city population, aggregate manufacturing in up to 114 cities, and eight industries. Under a unique equilibrium shock and recovery growth lie on one slope −1 line through the origin; under multiple equilibria on parallel lines with ordered intercepts. At every level the data prefer a unique stable equilibrium; the best multiple-equilibria fits violate the intercept-ordering criterion. Industry recovery is slower where hit hardest. Read in part. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1694](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1694.md) | Tong — TASI Lectures on Solitons | Read in part, for one mechanism. A finite-energy configuration must reach a vacuum at infinity; the maps from the boundary into the vacua fall into homotopy classes, which split configurations into sectors labelled by a charge measured as a surface term at the boundary, and the energy (or action, or tension) in a sector is bounded below by the charge, the soliton saturating the bound. A kink interpolates between distinct vacua at the two ends. Vortex-antivortex pairs annihilate. That such solitons can end only by annihilation or by a change at the boundary is the reader's inference from these points, not Tong's sentence. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1698](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1698.md) | Fodor — Radiation of oscillons | Read in part. Exactly periodic localized solutions of a real scalar exist only for the 1+1 sine-Gordon breather; every other oscillon radiates, at a rate exponentially small in its amplitude parameter but nonzero. Stability follows from whether total energy rises with central amplitude: in 3+1 dimensions oscillons are stable only above a minimum amplitude and, carried below it by radiation, suddenly decay after a few thousand oscillations; in 1 and 2 dimensions they never decay. Lifetimes under fine-tuning are limited by numerical precision, and whether the fine-tuned states are permanent is contested by Gleiser & Krackow (2019), not cited in the review and left unresolved here. | Skimmed |
